messages:
anna: quick summary — did a targeted staging run to validate per-key burst behavior vs per-org quotas. noticed weird cluster of 429s for some API keys but not others. posting logs + config we used and a short set of asks.

loadtest-bot: run completed: id=run-2026-03-12-07 summary: total_reqs=50240 duration=600s rps=83.7 p50=90ms p95=220ms p99=480ms 429_count=902 (1.8%) 

jess: saw that in the raw logs too. 429s are concentrated on keys that start with "dev-". org-level quota looks healthy for the orgs involved.

miguel: did you use per-key token buckets or only org buckets for the test?

anna: per-key enabled. config we used:
```
rate_limiter:
  scope_priority: ["key", "org"]
  key_bucket: { refill_per_sec: 25, capacity: 200 }
  org_bucket: { refill_per_sec: 500, capacity: 2000 }
  burst_window_sec: 60
```

sophie: curious — console metrics show "requests.blocked" by org but no breakdown by API key. that makes debugging hard.

jess: attaching a short log excerpt (anonymized):
```
[2026-03-12T07:03:21Z] key=dev-42 req=chat.completions tokens=34 status=429 reason=rate_limited scope=key remaining=0 reset_in=18s
[2026-03-12T07:03:21Z] key=prod-7 req=chat.completions tokens=11 status=200
[2026-03-12T07:03:22Z] key=dev-42 req=chat.embeddings tokens=512 status=429 reason=burst_exhausted
```

miguel: two quick theories: 1) our per-key limiter does not correctly deduct KV-cache hits vs raw tokens so short requests consume more credits, 2) the routing path for certain keys hit the generic pool because of a shard mismatch. I'll instrument the limiter to emit "rate_limit.scope" tag per decision.

anna: great. another observation: when a key hits 429 we sometimes see fallback to a cheaper model routing which then also gets its own quota checks and sometimes fails faster. this cascade is burying the root cause.

sophie: UX ask — can we add a console toggle to show per-key rolling credits and a link from a 429 event to the last N requests for that key? would speed triage for customers.

jess: +1. for immediate triage I exported a per-key histogram to S3: s3://redwood-staging/rl-probes/2026-03-12/dev-dev-42-hist.json (shared in #eng-sre).

loadtest-bot: diagnostic summary: top 5 keys by 429s: [dev-42, dev-11, dev-7, sandbox-3, test-9]. avg burst_consumption_per_60s for dev-42 = 214 tokens.

miguel: I'll open a small patch to ensure we check key-bucket first and emit metrics:
- metric: rate_limit.decision (allowed/blocked)
- tags: scope=key|org, key_id=..., route=...

anna: action items:
- miguel: instrument and deploy limiter patch to staging (canary 10% traffic) — target: 1768005000
- sophie: prototype per-key credits chart in console and add link from 429 event — target: end of week
- jess: keep exporting the raw per-key histograms for next 3 runs
- anna: write run notes + open follow-up PR with test harness and config used (#2345)

sophie: tiny UX note — show both "burst credits" and "sustained rate" on the dashboard. customers confuse burst window with sustained limit a lot.

anna: thanks all. if anyone wants to pair on the canary rollout ping me. planning to do the canary tomorrow morning (UTC) and then run a 15m probe focusing on keys that previously tripped 429s. :thumbsup:

miguel: ack. I'll add an alert if per-key 429 rate > 0.5% for 2m during canary.

loadtest-bot: scheduled next_probe id=run-2026-03-13-03 starts=1768080000 expected_reqs=60000

anna: closing thread for now. will update when canary + results are in.
